title: A hyphen-grouped value near a HubSpot word with no hapikey carrier
summary: A synthetic five-group 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal value beside the word HubSpot in prose and alone on a line, with no hapikey parameter around it.
rationale: The only support for a hyphen-grouped 8-4-4-4-12 shape is consistency between two scanner rule artifacts (an existing tool-corroborated claim), and neither says which HubSpot credential the shape describes. HubSpot's own pages state no prefix, alphabet, length or grouping for the account key or the developer key, and a masked example gives none. So the shape is not a documented format, a bare value has no carrier, and a UUID-shaped string is also what many unrelated identifiers look like; whether such a value is the legacy key, the developer key, a later token or an identifier is open.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted: no HubSpot statement gives the format, the grouped shape rests on consistency between two scanner rule artifacts only, and a bare value has no documented carrier. A HubSpot statement of the key format, or a dated page showing which credential the grouping belongs to, would settle it. The positive Case for the hapikey query parameter does not depend on the shape.

sources.supports: The developer API key is given in the hapikey query parameter; the page states no format for it.
The page states no format, prefix or length for the account key or the developer key.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. No outcome is asserted: the open question named in the expectation is what would have to be settled first.
